title: Transportation Systems, Urban Mobility, Transit, ITS, and Logistics Foundations

sources.notes: MIT OCW Urban Transportation Planning course identity for policy, politics, planning, and engineering of urban transportation systems; federal/state/local/MPO roles; public transit in the automobile era; trends and pattern breaks; analytical tools; traffic engineering; policy analysis; air pollution, social costs, climate change, land-use/transport interaction, sustainability, instructor insights, notes, and problem sets.

MIT OCW urban transportation syllabus identity for Boston-region case context, institutional structure, process/outcome impacts, environment/economy/equity tradeoffs, pattern breaks, walking tours, public meetings/events, assignments, recitations, and local case-study boundaries.

MIT OCW Public Transportation Systems course identity for urban public transportation modes, bus and rail, data collection and analysis, performance monitoring, route design, frequency determination, vehicle and crew scheduling, pricing policy, service quality, ridership, lecture notes, and videos.

MIT OCW public transportation syllabus identity for technology characteristics, capacity, cost, proposed-service-change cost estimation, organizational delivery models, finance/operations, labor relations, fare policy/technology, marketing, operations management, problem sets, final exam, and reading boundaries.

MIT OCW Transportation Systems Analysis course identity for transportation demand and cost analysis, planning, investment, operations, maintenance, microeconomics, demand models, discrete choice, cost models, production functions, pricing theory, congestion pricing, technological change, finance, project evaluation, urban passenger, freight, aviation, and ITS.

MIT OCW transportation systems analysis syllabus identity for core Master of Science in Transportation scope, lectures, recitations, readings from textbooks/articles/papers, five problem sets, midterm, final exam, grading, academic honesty, and assignment collaboration boundaries.

MIT OCW Intelligent Transportation Systems course identity for ITS as a transition in transportation, surface-transportation information systems, communications, sensors, highways, public transportation, air-traffic-control comparison, lecture notes, project examples, written assignments, and textbook boundary.

MIT OCW ITS syllabus identity for ATIS, network operations, commercial vehicles, intermodal freight, public transportation applications, regional strategic planning and architectures, institutions, safety, security, deployment, R&D/business models, sustainable mobility, TDM, tolling, road pricing, mini term paper, and group regional architecture project.

MIT OCW Logistical and Transportation Planning Methods course identity for operations research techniques in transportation systems analysis, urban/air/ocean/highway/pickup-delivery systems, urban service systems, random variables, geometrical probability, multi-server queueing, spatial location theory, network/graph analysis, simulation, exams, notes, problem sets, solutions, and open textbook boundary.

MIT OCW logistical/transportation methods syllabus identity for course meeting times, Larson/Odoni Urban Operations Research textbook boundary, online prior edition boundary, quizzes, problem sets, and grading.
